universalRules: Body measure sits between roughly 55 and 75 characters, and it is the measure that is constrained, not the container. (marketing.md:84; redesign-audit.md:57)
Line-height scales inversely with size: display text needs proportionally less leading than body text. (redesign-audit.md:58)
Few type sizes, used hard. A page with nine sizes has a scale, not a hierarchy. (marketing.md:86)
What is inside a container is tighter than the container. A control that shares its card's corner reads as a mistake. State it without naming a value. (marketing.md:92-95; redesign-audit.md:89)
Spacing comes from one declared step and every value is a multiple of it. The step itself is the direction's to choose. (marketing.md:85; redesign-audit.md:94)
Motion never sits between an intent and its result. Nothing moves in a form; nothing delays a click. (marketing.md:128)
Transitions belong on transform and opacity. Animating geometry forces layout on every frame. (redesign-audit.md:113-114)
Hover is never the only affordance, because touch has no hover. (redesign-audit.md:102)
A disabled control carries the actual disabled attribute. Something that looks pressable and does nothing is a bug. (redesign-audit.md:106)
The pending state occupies the space the result will occupy, so nothing jumps when the result arrives. (redesign-audit.md:108)

An error appears inline, next to its cause, with a way forward. An empty state is composed, not a blank panel. A partial state exists for when some data arrived and some did not. (redesign-audit.md:110-112)
Anything the reader is asked to compare must not shift position on the axis of comparison. State the obligation, never the implementation. (redesign-audit.md:59,92,93)

Verify every import against the dependency manifest before writing it. (redesign-audit.md:165-166)
Content in a series varies the way real content varies: dates, lengths, authors, portraits. Uniformity across a set is the tell, even when each item passes on its own. (redesign-audit.md:134-135)

marketing.md is 30% appearance, not the 50% on record, and it should still be deleted — but the reason on record is wrong and will misfire on the next two mode files. Recount: the architecture cites six of twelve numbered decisions as appearance (first-screen arrangement, density, radius, imagery, motion, accent count). Three of those six are stale. Sections 2, 3 and 4 had already been rewritten into outcome form and now say the opposite of what is attributed to them: 'There is no default arrangement here' (l.47), 'The specific numbers come from the contract' (l.80), 'there is no marketing radius either' (l.98). The honest count is two decisions wholly appearance (6 Motion, 7 Colour emphasis), two majority appearance (9 Navigation, 11 Content density), one mixed (5 Imagery). About 3.5 of 12, roughly 31 of 168 body lines.

The deletion still stands, for two reasons that are not the recorded one. First, the concentrated 30% is the failed recipe itself: 'the accent appears in three places, not thirty' plus 'neutrals carry the page' is PALETTE-ANALYSIS finding 4 written as an obligation, and Nordrig build B executed exactly that. Second, this file already survived one round of prose self-restraint — sections 2 to 4 were rewritten to refuse defaults, the run still produced 0/8, and the untouched sections 6 and 7 are why. Prose restraint does not work on a file of this shape.

But the stated reason — 'a marketing-specific craft floor could only contain rules that are either universal or a look' — is falsified by the file. Four rules are neither: the six-beat argument shape (l.29-39), the proof ladder with 'nothing' as a legitimate rung (l.144-152), the delete-every-image-and-panel test (l.188-191), and the table mapping the subject's strongest true material to what the first screen is built around (l.57-64). None is universal (a dashboard makes no argument and needs no proof section) and none is a look. The fourth is a divergence engine, not a convergence risk. Delete the file, rescue those four into SKILL.md sections 6 and 7 rather than inventing a floor/decide.md, and correct the recorded reasoning before ecommerce.md and product-ui.md are judged by the same two-category argument.

redesign-audit.md is two documents. The four diagnostic tables (Passes 1, 2, 3, 6; ~60 lines) are 72% appearance — 28 of 39 rows — and are the redesign path's convergence engine. Pass 2 read top to bottom instructs every project to arrive at an off-black or off-white ground tinted toward one desaturated accent, one grey family, hue-tinted shadows and a noise layer. That is a complete house style shipped as an audit, and it is the same rule as marketing.md section 7 stated in a second file so that both the build path and the redesign path reach it. Pass 6 is the inverted version: prescribe one replacement per default globally and the alternatives become the new defaults. The remaining ~140 lines are 90% obligation and hold the strongest material in the whole v2 corpus: the preservation contract, read-score-repair phasing, the six states, the forgotten-surfaces checklist, the repair order and the scoring rubric. Build redesign.md from that half; move Pass 6's left column to a tells corpus and discard its right column. Two caveats carried forward: the tabular-figures rule is correct and complicit (it mandates one of the four round-8 devices through the obligations door), and the scoring rubric is proven insufficient in the exact dimension it measures, since all three converged sites passed its per-site Originality test while the portfolio failed.

setup.md is roughly 95% obligation and near-zero appearance — the purest floor material of the three and the most under-rated. Its decision gate, four-condition definition of a sufficient stack, build-before-design verification, API-key prohibition and 'never ship it at default styling' all have no home in v3 today. Fold it into stacks/static.md whole rather than silently.

The engineering finding that outranks all three: floor-lint.mjs passes marketing.md clean. Its only failure is a missing rendition heading. Meanwhile redesign-audit.md fails on five lines, four of which are quotations of defects it is telling you to remove. The lint's own model of appearance is 'a value someone could copy into a stylesheet', and that is not how round 8 converged: build B chose #0f1218 and #3dd6c6, values appearing nowhere in any v2 file, by executing a prescribed structure written in prose. Until the purity scan also bans prescribed devices, accent budgets, motion characters, nav dimensions, component substitutions and word counts, a rewritten floor can reproduce the failure and report green.
